The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f2aeefc98af1afcd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let p > n + 1 be prime. There exist an enumeration I1, . . . , I2n of the subsets of {1, . . . , n}, a filtration F•, and a family of classes yi ∈ π1−2iD, 1 ≤ i ≤ n, with the following properties. (a) Filtration and unit. The enumeration has I1 = ∅ and max Ij nondecreasing for j ≥ 2. The filtration is 0 = F0 −→ F1 −→ · · · −→ F2n ≃ − → Xn,p with cofib(Fj−1 → Fj) ≃ CIj , where C∅ = Ln−1S, CI = Σ−d(I) Ln−max IS (I ̸= ∅). (1.1) Under F1 = C∅, the composite F1 → Xn,p is the canonical localization unit. (b) Simultaneous product bases. For this one family, set y∅ = 1 and yI = yi1 · · · yir for I = {i1 < · · · < ir}. For every 1 ≤ t < n, the specified map LK(t)   _ I⊆{1,...,n−t} Σ−d(I) S (yI ) − − → D   is an equivalence. (1.2)
